title: Recent advances in the understanding of the repeated bout effect: the protective effect against muscle damage from a single bout of eccentric exercise
journal: Scandinavian Journal of Medicine & Science in Sports
population: Eccentric exercise literature on the repeated bout effect
findings: A single eccentric bout protects against muscle damage in later eccentric bouts (the repeated bout effect).
Proposed adaptations are neural, mechanical and cellular.

There is some evidence of a shift toward slow-twitch motor unit recruitment, evidence of increased dynamic and passive muscle stiffness with eccentric training, and evidence of longitudinal sarcomere addition and altered inflammatory response.
The effect occurs with electrically stimulated contractions, indicating that a peripheral, non-neural adaptation predominates.
limitations: Narrative review from 2003, with no running-specific or duration data. The abstract gives no dose or protection duration.
implications: Treat protection from a single downhill exposure as real but mechanism-unclear; schedule an early moderate downhill session before heavy ones.
Prescribe no specific protective dose from this paper; use it only to justify progression from short, moderate descents.

verification.notes: Crossref: Scand J Med Sci Sports 13(2):88-97, 2003, single author matches. Europe PMC PMID 12641640 abstract checked. Population changed from 'human and animal' (not in abstract). Review is not running-specific.
